analysis.title: GS Stankard - Eq Positioning and Key Levels 9 Nov 2026
key_insights: CTA baseline flow forecasts show about $23bn of global equity selling over the next week on a flat tape, with roughly $36bn of selling in North America, nearly all in SPX.

On a flat tape, CTAs are projected to sell $45.7bn of global equities over the next month, including $41.1bn out of SPX. An up tape flips the month to +$74bn of buying (+$14.4bn into SPX). A down tape implies -$149.5bn of selling (-$45.4bn out of SPX).
GS key pivot levels for SPX are 7,676 (short term), 7,549 (medium term) and 7,084 (long term).
GS Prime Brokerage data show global equities net sold (-1.0 SDs 1-year) as de-grossing sped up (-0.8 SDs 1-year, largest dollar de-grossing since July). Long sales outpaced short covers 5 to 1.
US Fundamental L/S net leverage fell 3.7 pts to 43.3%, the 0th percentile over five years. This was the largest weekly decline since the week of Liberation Day (Apr '25).
US Fundamental L/S gross leverage fell 8.7 pts to 207.5% (26th percentile 1-year), the largest weekly decline since March 2020.

Overall book net leverage fell 1.8 pts to 71.8% (4th percentile 1-year) and the L/S ratio fell 1.2% to 1.592 (3rd percentile 1-year), while overall gross leverage rose 0.1 pts to 314.2% (85th percentile 1-year).

Info Tech was by far the most net sold global and US sector this week, across all regions, with long and short sales at 2.2 to 1. In percentage terms the selling matched mid-October and Sep '24 as the largest on record since 2016. Four of the top five net selling weeks in global Info Tech on record fall within the past five months.

Industrials was the second most net sold global sector. It was net sold for a 4th straight week and saw the largest percentage net selling in over 5 years. Electrical Equipment, Building Products and Aerospace & Defense led the subsector selling.
US single stocks saw the largest net selling in more than 4 months (-2.1 SDs 1-year), with long and short sales at 3.8 to 1. Global single stocks were net sold for an 8th straight week.

Macro Products (index and ETF) were net bought for a 2nd straight week in the US (+1.5 SDs 1-year). US-listed ETF shorts rose 7% on Nov 5, the largest 1-day increase since March, and 3.3% week over week, led by Large Cap Equity ETFs.
Buyback desk mix shifted to 33% open market vs 67% 10b5-1, from 22%/78% the prior week. About 90% of the S&P 500 is in its open window, with about 93% expected by the end of the week.

Desk buyback volumes were 1.6x 2025 YTD ADTV and 1.7x 2024 YTD ADTV, led by Industrials, Financials and Energy. 2026 YTD buyback authorizations reached $1.5T, above the 2025 full-year total of $1.37T.

The GS Fundamental L/S Performance Estimate fell 1.48% from 10/30 to 11/5 against MSCI World TR at -3.55%. Beta contributed -2.07% and alpha +0.60%. The Systematic L/S estimate fell 0.61%, with alpha of -1% and beta of +0.39%.

sector_views.rationale: Hedge funds net sold the sector across all regions. Global Tech net selling was on par with the largest weeks on record since 2016, and 4 of the top 5 weeks have come in the past five months. This is a positioning observation, not a GS rating.
The sector was net sold for a 4th straight week, with the largest percentage net selling in over 5 years. This is a positioning observation, not a GS rating.
These were the most net bought US sectors this week. This is a flow observation, not a GS rating.

earnings_insights: Q3 reporting is still in progress, and about 90% of the S&P 500 is in its buyback open window as of the report, with about 93% expected by the end of the week.
Buyback desk activity was driven by the post-election period and an active earnings calendar. No company-level EPS or revenue figures are given.
risk_factors: CTA selling is forecast under every one-week scenario and under flat and down tapes over one month, so systematic supply is a headwind unless the market rallies.
Hedge fund net leverage is at multi-year lows, and US Fundamental L/S net leverage is at the 0th percentile over five years.
Tech selling is concentrated and repeated, with 4 of the top 5 net selling weeks on record in the past five months.
The rise in ETF shorts on Nov 5 was the largest 1-day increase since March, which signals added index-level hedging or bearish positioning.
vol_and_positioning: CTA pivot levels for SPX are 7,676 (short term), 7,549 (medium term) and 7,084 (long term). A 1x std-dev market move is 1.62% over 1 week and 3.78% over 1 month.
CTA 1-week flows: flat tape -$23.3bn (-$31.1bn out of SPX), up tape -$3.9bn (-$23.1bn out of SPX), down tape -$48.7bn (-$31.5bn out of SPX).
Overall book net leverage is 71.8% (4th percentile 1-year), L/S ratio is 1.592 (3rd percentile 1-year), and gross leverage is 314.2% (85th percentile 1-year).
Fundamental L/S net leverage is 45.3% (2nd percentile 5-year). Beta-adjusted Fundamental L/S net leverage is 57.2% (4th percentile 3-year).
US-listed ETF shorts rose 7% on Nov 5, the largest 1-day rise since March (3rd largest in 5 years), led by shorting in Large Cap Equity ETFs.
Single stocks were net sold for an 8th straight week while Macro Products were net bought for a 3rd straight week globally.

tension_points.bull_case: Corporate buybacks are accelerating. The open window covers about 90% of the S&P 500 and rises to about 93% this week, YTD authorizations are $1.5T, and desk volumes are 1.6x the 2025 YTD average. An up tape would flip CTA flows to +$74bn of buying over one month.
tension_points.bear_case: CTAs are projected to sell $23.3bn of global equities over one week on a flat tape and $149.5bn over one month on a down tape. Hedge funds are de-grossing, with US Fundamental L/S net leverage at the 0th percentile over five years, and Tech and Industrials selling is at record or multi-year extremes.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The SPX medium-term pivot at 7,549 and the long-term pivot at 7,084 mark where CTA selling would intensify. A move above the 7,676 short-term pivot would shift the flat-tape CTA flow toward buying.
